newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol reaffirms Latam expansion strategy.
newsitem.headline: Repsol reaffirms Latam expansion strategy.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol on Friday reaffirmed expectations of strong growth in the next five years, as well as a strategy to expand in Latin America.

Addressing the annual shareholders' meeting, Chairman Alfonso Cortina said strategy would also continue to concentrate on developing the electricity business in Spain, strengthening growth of exploration and production, and maintaining its leading position at home.
Although the firm was aware that investment in Latin America was more risky, Repsol considers it can benefit from the continent's high growth rates.
"(Latin American growth rates) are not comparable with those in Spain, and although the risks are bigger, we believe it is under control," Cortina said.

The firm aims to target Latin America, "in particular integrating operations including production, refining, transport and marketing, including power generation, in new markets with large population centres", according to the annual report, which adds that further acquisitions in Latin America are under study.
Cortina told shareholders that one aim of the company was to increase its oil reserves so as to better use the firm's refining capacity.

"We must confess that compared with other firms of our size, Repsol does not have sufficient weight within its assets corresponding to petrol reserves as our refining capacity would suggest," he said.
At today's meeting, shareholders voted to authorise the board to issue convertible bonds, with or without preferential subscription rights, or raise capital if necessary.
Cortina told shareholders the board had requested this to make the company "sufficiently flexible in case an unexpected investment opportunity comes up."
Nevertheless, in his first shareholder meeting at the head of the fully privatised energy group, Cortina reaffirmed that there were no concrete plan to issue bonds.

In answer to shareholder questions, Cortina said the firm's debt levels were growing, although "always maintaining assumable limits and ratios which have given us our currency ratings from international ratings agencies."

The shareholders' meeting also approved a dividend of 181 pesetas gross per share paid against 1996 results, up six percent from the year earlier. The final dividend of 102 pesetas is effective July 1.
The firm is committed to keeping payout at 40-50 percent, Cortina said.
